current_bottleneck: 641a's failure is not global underdispersion. Temperature improves coverage and pathwise max-jump KS but damages conditionality, kurtosis, per-cell tail scale, level placement, and cross-cell coherence. The bottleneck is state/cell/horizon-specific conditional probability allocation inside the unified path law.
last_result_summary: 643a ran an evaluation-only sample-temperature sweep on 641a. Baseline temp 1.00 scored 4/11 with cov90 0.647, kurtosis ratio 0.946, q99 pass 23/25, cross corr 0.949, path KS 0.610. Temp 1.10 scored 3/11: cov90 0.679 and path KS 0.518, but conditional MAE dropped to 2.46%, kurtosis ratio failed at 0.739, q99 pass fell to 20/25, and cross corr fell to 0.766. Temp 1.25 also scored 3/11: cov90 0.710 and path KS 0.314, but conditional MAE was ~0%, daily KS fell to 16/25, level KS 2/25, median pass 5/25, kurtosis 0.515, q99 pass 11/25, and cross corr 0.513.
next_step_recommendation: Close scalar temperature as a risk-policy calibration for 641a. The next step is research ideation for objective/calibration changes that allocate conditional location/spread by state, cell, and horizon while preserving one unified IV+anchor-factor path law. Do not add more sampling knobs or separate factor treatments.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
